questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹41, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years are given, the principal can be calculated directly:

Principal = (SI)² ÷ (4 × Difference)

Difference between CI and SI = 41 − 40 = ₹1

Principal = (40 × 40) ÷ (4 × 1) = 1600 ÷ 4 = 400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

questions.question: The average age of 52 students of a class is 12 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 13 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a new member joins and the average increases, the new value can be calculated directly:

Teacher's Age = Old Average + (Total Members × Increase in Average)

Teacher's Age = 12 + (53 × 1)

Teacher's Age = 12 + 53 = 65

**∴ The correct answer is 65 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 52

Average age of students = 12 years

New average age including the teacher = 13 years

Total members including the teacher = 52 + 1 = 53

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 Teacher's Age = Old Average + (Total Persons × Increase in Average)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ages of 52 students = 52 × 12 = 624 years

⇒ Sum of ages of 53 members = 53 × 13 = 689 years

⇒ Teacher's age = Sum of ages of 53 members − Sum of ages of 52 students

⇒ Teacher's age = 689 − 624 = 65 years

**∴ The correct answer is 65 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Averages (Net Deviation)

If a new value is added and the average increases, the new value is greater than the old average by an amount equal to (Total observations × increase in average).

Averages (Removal)

If a value is removed and the average decreases, the removed value was strictly greater than the old average of the group.

Combined Average

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂) where n is the number of items and A is the average of each respective group.

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP). It is calculated as Profit = SP − CP. Conversely, Loss occurs when CP is greater than SP, and is calculated as Loss = CP − SP.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is typically calculated on the Cost Price (unless specifically stated otherwise). The formula is: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Unitary Method Application

To find the total value for a specific number of items, first calculate the value of a single unit by dividing the total value by its total quantity. Then, multiply this single unit value by the required quantity.

questions.question: The LCM of 44, 32, 176 and 352 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the largest number in the given set, which is 352.

Check if 352 is perfectly divisible by the other given numbers:

352 ÷ 44 = 8 | 352 ÷ 32 = 11 | 352 ÷ 176 = 2

Since the largest number is perfectly divisible by all the other numbers, it is their LCM.

**∴ The correct answer is 352.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 44, 32, 176, and 352

**Concept Used:**

In the prime factorisation method, the LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the given numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 44 = 2² × 11

⇒ 32 = 2⁵

⇒ 176 = 2⁴ × 11

⇒ 352 = 2⁵ × 11

⇒ LCM = Highest power of 2 × Highest power of 11

⇒ LCM = 2⁵ × 11

⇒ LCM = 32 × 11 = 352

**∴ The correct answer is 352.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest common divisor that completely divides two or more given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b': a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).
</p

questions.question: Suman covers a certain distance by car, driving at 22 km/hr, and he returns to the starting point, riding on a scooter at a speed of 17 km/hr. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:

When the distance covered is the same for two parts of a journey, use the direct formula:

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 22 × 17) ÷ (22 + 17)

⇒ Average Speed = 748 ÷ 39 = 19 ⁷/₃₉ km/hr

questions.question: In a circular race of 500 m, A and B start from the same point and at the same time at speeds of 36 km/hr and 45 km/hr in the same direction. After how long will they meet again for the first time on the track?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert speeds to m/s: A = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s, B = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s.

Because they run in the same direction, Relative Speed = 12.5 − 10 = 2.5 m/s.

Time to meet = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ 2.5 = 200 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 200 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

questions.question: Vipul invests a sum of ₹5400 and Vijay invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 5 years, Vijay gets ₹480 more interest than Vipul, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Total difference in interest for 5 years = ₹480

Difference in interest for 1 year = 480 ÷ 5 = ₹96

Rate of interest (R) = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal difference) × 100

⇒ R = (96 ÷ 4000) × 100 = 2.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.4%.**

Principal for Vipul = ₹5400

Principal for Vijay = ₹9400

Time (T) = 5 years

Difference in Simple Interest = ₹480

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

questions.question: The mean proportional of 0.5 and 72 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The mean proportional between any two numbers 'a' and 'b' is calculated directly using the formula √(a × b).

Mean proportional = √(0.5 × 72)

Mean proportional = √36

Mean proportional = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two provided numbers are a = 0.5 and b = 72.

**Formula Used:**

If three quantities are in continued proportion such that a : x :: x : b, then x is considered the mean proportional between a and b.

Product of extremes = Product of means ⇒ x² = a × b

 
 0.5

 :

 
 x

 ::

 
 x

 :

 
 72

 Mean Proportional (x) = √(a × b)
 x = √(0.5 × 72) = 6

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required mean proportional be x.

⇒ 0.5 ÷ x = x ÷ 72

⇒ x² = 0.5 × 72

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is called the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is the fourth proportional to a, b, and c. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Continued Proportion

Three non-zero quantities a, b, and c of the same kind are said to be in continued proportion if the ratio of a to b is absolutely equal to the ratio of b to c.
</p

questions.question: A company offers a buy 2 get 1 free scheme on pens priced at ₹10 each. What is the effective discount percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any Buy X Get Y Free scheme, the discount percentage is always calculated on the total number of items.

Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

⇒ Discount % = [1 ÷ (2 + 1)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33¹/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 33¹/₃%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

• 
 Selling Price (2 pens) = ₹20

**Given:**

Marked price of 1 pen = ₹10

Scheme: Buy 2 get 1 free

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of pens received = 2 (bought) + 1 (free) = 3

⇒ Total Marked Price (MP) of 3 pens = 3 × 10 = ₹30

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for the customer (paying only for 2 pens) = 2 × 10 = ₹20

⇒ Discount amount = MP − SP = 30 − 20 = ₹10

⇒ Discount % = (10 ÷ 30) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100 ÷ 3 = 33¹/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 33¹/₃%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Rule

The effective discount is always calculated on the total number of items taken out of the shop. Effective Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP), not the Cost Price (CP). Therefore, Selling Price = Marked Price × [(100 − Discount %) ÷ 100].

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount percentage is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: One-third of a work is finished in four days by P and one-fourth of the same work is finished in six days by Q. P and Q together work for six days and the rest of the work is finished by R in two days. R alone can finish the whole work in _____ days.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time taken by P to finish the whole work = 4 × 3 = 12 days, and Q = 6 × 4 = 24 days.

Let Total Work = LCM(12, 24) = 24 units.

Efficiency of P = 2 units/day, Q = 1 unit/day ⇒ P + Q = 3 units/day.

Work done by P and Q in 6 days = 6 × 3 = 18 units.

Remaining work = 24 − 18 = 6 units, which is done by R in 2 days ⇒ R's efficiency = 3 units/day.

Time taken by R alone to complete the work = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete 1/3 of the work = 4 days

Time taken by Q to complete 1/4 of the work = 6 days

Time worked by P and Q together = 6 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time taken by P to complete the whole work = 4 × 3 = 12 days

⇒ Total time taken by Q to complete the whole work = 6 × 4 = 24 days

 **Days**

 **Efficiency**

⇒ Combined efficiency of (P + Q) = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Total work completed by P and Q in 6 days = 6 × 3 = 18 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done = 24 − 18 = 6 units

⇒ R finishes the remaining 6 units in 2 days, so the Efficiency of R = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 units/day

⇒ Time taken by R alone to finish the whole work (24 units) = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

Functions exactly like Time and Work, but an outlet pipe has a negative efficiency. If an inlet fills the tank in X hours and an outlet empties it in Y hours, the net filling capacity in 1 hour is (1/X − 1/Y).

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in direct proportion to the actual amount of work done by each person. If all persons work for the same number of days, the total wages are divided directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

If two people A and B work on alternate days, find the combined work done in a single 2-day cycle. Then multiply this cycle to approach the total work closely before calculating the time needed to finish the remainder.

questions.question: What will be the surface area of the sphere having 5.4 cm radius?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The surface area of a sphere is calculated directly using the formula 4πr².

Square the given radius: 5.4 × 5.4 = 29.16.

Multiply by 4: 29.16 × 4 = 116.64.

Append π to obtain the final surface area.

**∴ The correct answer is 116.64 π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (r) = 5.4 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a Sphere = 4 × π × r²

 
 

 

 
• 
 
 r = 5.4 cm
 Surface Area = 4 × π × r²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × (5.4)²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × 29.16

⇒ Surface Area = 116.64 π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 116.64 π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The total volume enclosed by a solid sphere is determined by the formula: V = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r³.

Curved Surface Area of a Hemisphere

When a sphere is cut perfectly in half, the resulting curved surface area is exactly half of the full sphere: CSA = 2 × π × r².

Total Surface Area of a Hemisphere

By including the flat circular base, the total surface area of a solid hemisphere becomes: TSA = 3 × π × r².

questions.question: Find the ratio between the third proportional of 32 and 48 with the third proportional of 4 and 18.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Third proportional to a and b is b² ÷ a.

First proportional = 48² ÷ 32 = 72

Second proportional = 18² ÷ 4 = 81

Required Ratio = 72 : 81 = 8 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First pair of numbers: 32 and 48

Second pair of numbers: 4 and 18

**Formula Used:**

If *c* is the third proportional to *a* and *b*, then *c* = *b*² ÷ *a*

 
 First Pair
 32 and 48
 c1 = 72
 
 
 Second Pair
 4 and 18
 c2 = 81
 
 

 

 
 
 Ratio = 8 : 9

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let c₁ be the third proportional of 32 and 48.

⇒ c₁ = (48 × 48) ÷ 32 = 2304 ÷ 32 = 72

⇒ Let c₂ be the third proportional of 4 and 18.

⇒ c₂ = (18 × 18) ÷ 4 = 324 ÷ 4 = 81

⇒ Required Ratio = c₁ : c₂ = 72 : 81

⇒ Simplifying the ratio by dividing both sides by 9, we get 8 : 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Third Proportional

If a : b :: b : c, then c is called the third proportional to a and b. Formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If a : b :: c : d, then d is the fourth proportional to a, b and c. Formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).
</p

questions.question: There are four equilateral triangles with sides 95 cm, 76 cm, 57 cm and 152 cm. What maximum size scale (in cm) can measure all of them exactly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The maximum exact measuring scale size is the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the given lengths.

Given lengths: 57, 76, 95, 152.

Shortcut to find HCF: Check the minimum difference between any two given sorted numbers.

Minimum difference = 76 − 57 = 19.

Since 19 perfectly divides all the given numbers, it is the HCF.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the equilateral triangles = 95 cm, 76 cm, 57 cm, and 152 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Maximum size scale = HCF(95, 76, 57, 152)

 Maximum Scale = HCF(57, 76, 95, 152)

 76 cm

 152 cm

**Calculations:**

Let's find the prime factorization of each given number:

⇒ 57 = 3 × 19

⇒ 76 = 2 × 2 × 19 = 2² × 19

⇒ 95 = 5 × 19

⇒ 152 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 19 = 2³ × 19

The highest common factor present in all the numbers is 19.

⇒ HCF = 19

Thus, the maximum size of the scale required to measure exactly all these sides is 19 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest number that exactly divides two or more given numbers. It is strictly used in problems asking for "maximum size", "longest tape", or "equal largest portions".

Difference Method for HCF

The HCF of a set of numbers is either the smallest difference between any two numbers in the set, or a factor of that difference. This method serves as a highly effective shortcut for competitive exams.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest number that is a multiple of all given numbers. Used heavily in "meeting point", "bells ringing together", or "circular track" type problems.

Equilateral Triangle

A triangle in which all three sides have the identical length. Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a² and Perimeter = 3 × a, where 'a' represents the side length.

questions.question: Hari travels from City A to City B. If Hari drives his car at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 30 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Hari would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a constant distance, Speed and Time are inversely proportional.

Speed ratio (New : Normal) = 2 : 3 ⇒ Time ratio (New : Normal) = 3 : 2

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Given, the delay is 1 unit = 30 minutes.

Normal time corresponds to 2 units ⇒ 2 × 30 = 60 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 minutes.**

questions.question: The cost price of an article is increased by 15% and later the new price is decreased by 15%. If the latest price of the article is ₹19,550, find the original cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a value is increased by x% and then decreased by x%, there is always a net decrease of (x² ÷ 100)%.

Net percentage change = −(15 × 15) ÷ 100 = −2.25%.

Final price is (100 − 2.25)% = 97.75% of original CP.

97.75% of CP = ₹19,550

CP = (19550 × 100) ÷ 97.75 = ₹20,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase = 15%

Percentage decrease = 15%

Latest price = ₹19,550

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + Rate₁/100) × (1 − Rate₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Equal Successive Increase and Decrease

If a number is first increased by x% and then decreased by x%, there is always an overall decrease. The net decrease percentage is x² ÷ 100.

Multiplier / Ratio Method

This method is highly efficient for complex fractional percentages. Convert each percentage change into a fraction and multiply the initial value by all the respective multiplying factors to instantly arrive at the final value.

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹80, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for Principal when 2-year Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) are given:

P = (SI)² ÷ [4 × (CI − SI)]

⇒ P = (40)² ÷ [4 × (80 − 40)]

⇒ P = 1600 ÷ [4 × 40]

⇒ P = 1600 ÷ 160 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 1st Yr SI: ₹20

 
 2nd Yr SI: ₹20

 Total CI = 20 + 20 + 40 = ₹80

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹40

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹80

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = ₹20

⇒ In Compound Interest, additional interest is earned on the 1st year's interest during the 2nd year.

⇒ Total Compound Interest = 1st year SI + 2nd year SI + Interest on 1st year SI

⇒ 80 = 20 + 20 + Interest on 1st year SI

⇒ Interest on 1st year SI = 80 − 40 = ₹40

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest on 1st year SI ÷ 1st year SI) × 100

⇒ R = (40 ÷ 20) × 100 = 200%

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = (Principal × R × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = (P × 200) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = 2P

⇒ P = 10

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for two years is directly calculated as D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

For a period of three years, the formula extends to D = P × (R ÷ 100)² × [(300 + R) ÷ 100].

Ratio of CI and SI for 2 Years

The relationship between Compound Interest and Simple Interest over exactly two years can be expressed as CI ÷ SI = (200 + R) ÷ 200.
